## Fresh developments (last 24–72 h)

### Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM pricing: decelerating, still positive
- **DigiTimes Jul 7**: "Memory prices defy cooling hopes" — sellers pushing fresh Q3 contract hikes on AI server demand despite consumer weakness. TrendForce Jul 3 Q3 print: conventional DRAM **+13–18% QoQ** (vs. +93–98% Q1, +58–63% Q2). Memflation compressing sharply on base effects; Jefferies more hawkish at +40–50%.
- HBM3e +20% QoQ late-June print (Silicon Analysts). HBM4 ~$500/stack — not yet settled annual contracts.

### Signal 2 — HBM4 ramp / correction risk
- **SK Hynix throttling HBM4** (Jun 24): diverting wafers to DDR5 where margins ~90% — HBM4 ramp pushed Q2→Q3. Paradoxically bullish for pricing duration; gives Samsung a rare catch-up window.
- **Micron**: entered HVM of HBM4 (36 GB, 12-stack) for NVIDIA Vera Rubin — official IR release. All three suppliers NVIDIA-certified for Vera Rubin.
- TrendForce (Jun 2): HBM prices "expected to surge multiples higher in 2027." No credible correction before 2027–2028.

### Signal 3 — Hyperscaler capex: $725B 2026, zero guide-downs
- Amazon ~$200B, Microsoft ~$190B, Alphabet ~$180–190B (raised), Meta ~$125–145B (raised). Aggregate **$725B (+77% YoY)**. Q1 prints all maintained/raised. Goldman projects $5.3T cumulative FY2025–FY2030. **No first-guide-down signal from any hyperscaler.** Note: capex-to-AI-revenue gap widening (~$600B) — Forbes Jun 2 flags markets beginning to reprice this.

### Signal 4 — NVIDIA Kyber NVL144 delay (BIGGEST 72h story)
- **Jul 6 (SemiAnalysis)**: NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale system delayed ~12 months to 2028 due to a 78-layer PCB midplane manufacturing failure. Asian chip stocks sold off immediately.
- **NVIDIA denied** the delay Jul 7; said roadmap is "intact." Goldman Sachs simultaneously called NVDA "compelling at 21.7x forward P/E" (vs. 5-yr avg 72x). Stock recovered ~1%+.
- **Samsung Q2 (Jul 7)**: 19× YoY profit jump but missed lofty AI expectations → **SOXX −6%, AMD −8%, MU −8%, INTC −10%, AMAT −10%** in a single session.
- **Goldman raised AMD PT to $640** (Jul 6); AMD Advancing AI 2026 keynote Jul 22–23 (Helios rack, MI450 commercial) is the next binary.
- **AVGO**: Multi-year Apple custom ASIC agreement through 2031 (8-K), stock +4.2%.
- **MRVL**: Jul 6 "chasing Broadcom's AI jackpot" (247 Wall St); NVLink Fusion + $2B NVIDIA invest intact; ex-div Jul 10.
- **CRDO**: Jul 6 — Evercore ISI Outperform $325, Stifel $350, BofA $340; FY2026 rev +205% YoY to $1.3B.

### Signal 5 — Optical: sector selloff, fundamentals intact
- **CIEN −8.65% Jul 2**, **COHR ~−15% off highs (~$314)**, **LITE −4.4% Jul 7** — AI-infra valuation derating, not fundamental. COHR orders booked to 2028 (Raymond James PT $435). LITE 700% YTD, $3.17B cash.
- InP: partial China easing (May batch shipped), prices still +200% YTD. CPO: NVIDIA Spectrum-X Photonics (Ethernet CPO) H2 2026 target — still <1% penetration.

### Signal 6 — Solar
- **ENPH**: Barclays upgraded Underweight→Equalweight (PT $30→$51), new AI-datacenter solid-state transformer (SST) TAM thesis (~$2B by decade-end). Q2 earnings Jul 28.
- **FSLR**: Wells Fargo PT $255→$320. Q2 earnings Jul 23/30. Key binary: Section 232 polysilicon probe early August.
- **ARRY** Barclays upgraded (record $2.4B orderbook). **NXT** downgraded despite Q3 beat (EPS $1.10 vs $0.94 est) on valuation.

## Context vs. baseline
Hyperscaler capex $725B now above baseline ceiling of $600–700B — no slowdown signal. Memory: both legs intact — conventional DRAM still rising and HBM sold out through 2026; SK Hynix HBM4 throttle extends supply tightness. NVIDIA Kyber delay (denied) is the first hint of execution risk in the Vera Rubin/Rubin Ultra roadmap — worth watching. Custom ASIC share shift accelerating (AVGO Apple deal, CRDO upgrades, MRVL NVLink). Optical pullback is sentiment noise; COHR booked to 2028. ENPH AI-SST angle is new vs. baseline.

## Most important development
**Samsung Q2 miss → global chip sector selloff (Jul 7)** is the defining event of the 72h window: SOXX −6%, AMD −8%, MU −8% in a single session, triggered by Samsung's 19× profit beat being "not good enough" for AI-stretched valuations. This is the first significant valuation reset of the cycle — **but the underlying AI demand signal (memory prices still rising, hyperscaler capex $725B, COHR orders booked to 2028) remains intact**. The NVIDIA Kyber NVL144 delay report (denied) is the second key event, adding execution risk to the Vera Rubin roadmap. AMD Jul 22–23 keynote is the next binary.
